subproblem.title: Transport of supported tensor relations to a restricted module
subproblem.statement: Let k and D be commutative rings, let D be a k-algebra, and let M and P be D-modules with additive commutative group structures. Fix a k-subalgebra A⊆D and an A-submodule N⊆M, using restricted D-actions throughout. Write G=FreeAbelianGroup(M×P) and [u,z] for its pair generator. Let T(A,N) consist of all [0,z] with z∈P; [u,0] with u∈N; [u+v,z]−[u,z]−[v,z] with u,v∈N and z∈P; [u,z+w]−[u,z]−[u,w] with u∈N and z,w∈P; and [d•u,z]−[u,d•z] with d∈A, u∈N and z∈P. For every m∈N and p∈P, if [m,p] belongs to the additive subgroup of G generated by T(A,N), then m⊗_A p=0 in N⊗_A P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {k : Type*} [CommRing k] {D : Type*} [CommRing D] [Algebra k D] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module D M] {P : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module D P] (A : Subalgebra k D) (N : Submodule A M) (m : N) (p : P), let b : M → P → FreeAbelianGroup (M × P) := fun u z => FreeAbelianGroup.of (u, z); b (m : M) p ∈ AddSubgroup.closure {r : FreeAbelianGroup (M × P) | (∃ z : P, r = b 0 z) ∨ (∃ u : M, u ∈ N ∧ r = b u 0) ∨ (∃ (u v : M) (z : P), u ∈ N ∧ v ∈ N ∧ r = b (u + v) z - b u z - b v z) ∨ (∃ (u : M) (z w : P), u ∈ N ∧ r = b u (z + w) - b u z - b u w) ∨ (∃ (d : D) (u : M) (z : P), d ∈ A ∧ u ∈ N ∧ r = b (d • u) z - b u (d • z))} → (TensorProduct.tmul A m p : TensorProduct A N P) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Fix all the stated data and let R be the subgroup generated by T(A,N). Finite integer linear combinations of elements of T(A,N) form a subgroup: the empty sum gives zero, concatenation gives addition, and negating coefficients gives additive inverses. This subgroup contains T(A,N), and every subgroup containing T(A,N) contains these combinations. Hence it equals R. The hypothesis therefore gives a finite formal identity [m,p]=∑_{i=1}^n c_i r_i in G, where each c_i is an integer and each r_i has one of the five forms defining T(A,N). Choose such a form and its operands for each r_i.
2. Put G_N=FreeAbelianGroup(N×P). Lift the first coordinates of the chosen relations to N. The zero-left relation lifts to [0,z], and a zero-right relation lifts to [ũ,0]. A first-coordinate additivity relation lifts to [ũ+ṽ,z]−[ũ,z]−[ṽ,z]; a second-coordinate additivity relation lifts to [ũ,z+w]−[ũ,z]−[ũ,w]. The required lifts exist because the chosen u and v belong to N and N is closed under addition and contains zero. For a balancing relation, d∈A gives a=⟨d,hd⟩ in A, and its lift is [a•ũ,z]−[ũ,a•z]. Restricted scalar actions give (a•ũ:M)=d•u and a•z=d•z. Thus all these lifted relations have precisely their chosen original forms after inclusion. Equalities between lifts follow from injectivity of subtype inclusion.
3. The inclusion i:N×P→M×P induces an additive homomorphism J:G_N→G sending every pair generator to the generator of its included pair. If r̃_i denotes the lifted relation from step 2, then J(r̃_i)=r_i. Also J([m,p]) is the original [m,p] in G.
4. The homomorphism J is injective. Indeed, write an element of G_N as its finitely supported integer coefficient function on N×P. Because i is injective, the coefficient of J(h) at i(t) is exactly the coefficient of h at t: no distinct pair contributes at i(t). Thus J(h)=0 implies that every coefficient of h is zero, and hence h=0. Applying this to the difference of any two elements proves injectivity.
5. By step 1 and preservation of finite sums and integer multiples, J([m,p])=J(∑ c_i r̃_i). Injectivity yields [m,p]=∑ c_i r̃_i already in G_N. Evaluate a pair generator [n,z] as n⊗_A z, extending to an additive homomorphism G_N→N⊗_A P. The zero, additivity and A-balancing identities of the tensor product kill all five types of lifted relations from step 2. Therefore the right side evaluates to zero and the left side evaluates to m⊗_A p. This proves the required equality.
proof_key_steps: Express membership in the supported relation subgroup as a finite integer combination.
Lift each zero, additivity and balancing relation using the submodule operations and restricted scalar actions.
Show that inclusion of pair generators induces an injective free-abelian-group map.
Use injectivity to lift the formal identity.
Evaluate in the smaller tensor product, where all lifted relations vanish.

subproblem.title: Kernel presentation of a tensor product by additive relations
subproblem.statement: Let D be a commutative ring and let M and P be D-modules with additive commutative group structures. Write G = FreeAbelianGroup(M × P) and [u,z] for its pair generator. Let T consist of all [0,z], [u,0], [u+v,z]−[u,z]−[v,z], [u,z+w]−[u,z]−[u,w], and [d•u,z]−[u,d•z], with u,v in M, z,w in P, and d in D. Let E:G→M⊗_D P be the additive homomorphism sending [u,z] to u⊗_D z. Then ker E is the additive subgroup generated by T.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {D : Type*} [CommRing D] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module D M] {P : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module D P], let b : M → P → FreeAbelianGroup (M × P) := fun u z => FreeAbelianGroup.of (u, z); (FreeAbelianGroup.lift (fun x : M × P => TensorProduct.tmul D x.1 x.2)).ker = AddSubgroup.closure {r : FreeAbelianGroup (M × P) | (∃ z : P, r = b 0 z) ∨ (∃ u : M, r = b u 0) ∨ (∃ (u v : M) (z : P), r = b (u + v) z - b u z - b v z) ∨ (∃ (u : M) (z w : P), r = b u (z + w) - b u z - b u w) ∨ (∃ (d : D) (u : M) (z : P), r = b (d • u) z - b u (d • z))}
subproblem.natural_proof:
1. Fix D, M and P as in the statement, and use its notation G, T and [u,z]. Let R be the additive subgroup generated by T. The universal property of the free abelian group gives the additive homomorphism E:G→M⊗_D P sending [u,z] to u⊗_D z.
2. Every generator in T is killed by E. For the two zero forms this follows from 0⊗z=0 and u⊗0=0; for the two additivity forms it follows from additivity of the tensor in the indicated argument; for the balancing form it follows from (d•u)⊗z=u⊗(d•z). Since ker E is a subgroup containing T, R is contained in ker E.
3. Form the quotient additive group Q=G/R with projection π. Set β(u,z)=π([u,z]). The first two types of generators give β(0,z)=0 and β(u,0)=0. The next two give β(u+v,z)=β(u,z)+β(v,z) and β(u,z+w)=β(u,z)+β(u,w). The last gives β(d•u,z)=β(u,d•z). Thus β is biadditive and D-balanced.
4. These identities induce an additive homomorphism L:M⊗_D P→Q with L(u⊗z)=β(u,z). Explicitly, extend β to the free additive monoid on pairs by summation. Its values agree across the zero, additivity and balancing constructors of the pinned TensorProduct.Eqv by step 3; they agree across its commutativity constructor because Q is abelian. The map therefore factors through the defining additive-congruence quotient. This is precisely TensorProduct.liftAddHom in the pinned library.
5. On each pair generator, (L∘E)([u,z])=π([u,z]). Additive homomorphisms out of a free abelian group are determined by generators, so L∘E=π on all of G: the equality extends to sums and additive inverses.
6. If g belongs to ker E, then π(g)=L(E(g))=L(0)=0. The zero class of G/R is exactly R, so g belongs to R. Hence ker E is contained in R. Together with step 2, this proves the asserted equality ker E=AddSubgroup.closure T.
proof_key_steps: Evaluate pair generators as pure tensors and show that every defining relation is killed.
In the quotient by the generated subgroup, pair classes form a biadditive balanced map.
Descend this map through the pinned tensor presentation to an additive map into the quotient.
Identify its composite with free-group evaluation as the quotient projection.
Use the kernel of the quotient projection to prove the reverse kernel inclusion.
